title: Validate and transform DNA sequences
intro: Begin sequence analysis by making ambiguity and reading-frame policies explicit before calculating molecular summaries.

scientific_context.caution: Short DNA strings are synthetic. A valid string is not a verified molecule, and translation does not establish biological expression.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → Investigate → Apply → independent Prove → delayed review.

goals.title: Validate bases and ambiguous N
goals.why: Ambiguous sequencing calls must not be silently counted as definitive nucleotides.
explain: Declare the alphabet before measuring. Treat N as unknown; do not replace it with A or delete the original sequence.
A string containing N may satisfy a permissive sequence policy but still have zero callable A/C/G/T bases.
The inputs are deliberately synthetic for practice; matching an expected result does not validate a biological interpretation.

worked_example.code:
seq='ACGNT'
allowed=set('ACGTN')
print(all(base in allowed for base in seq),seq.count('N'))
worked_example.predict: Does ACGNT satisfy the declared alphabet, and how many unknown calls remain?

goals.prediction_answer: True, one N; the permissive alphabet is not evidence of an A/C/G/T call.
walkthrough: Declare the alphabet before measuring. Treat N as unknown; do not replace it with A or delete the original sequence.
Build a set of accepted bases; enumerate the sequence instead of discarding unexpected positions.

goals.title: Calculate GC fraction with a declared denominator
goals.why: A GC percentage is misleading if N calls silently enlarge or shrink the denominator.
explain: Calculate GC/(A+C+G+T) among called bases; report None if none are called. A separate all-position fraction answers a different question.
Dividing by full read length silently treats unknown N bases as biologically known AT-like positions.
The inputs are deliberately synthetic for practice; matching an expected result does not validate a biological interpretation.

worked_example.code: s='GCNNAA';called=[b for b in s if b in 'ACGT'];print(sum(b in 'GC' for b in called)/len(called))
worked_example.predict: For GCNNAA, do the two Ns affect the denominator?

walkthrough: Calculate GC/(A+C+G+T) among called bases; report None if none are called. A separate all-position fraction answers a different question.
Count called A/C/G/T positions first; an all-N read has no defined called-base GC fraction.

goals.title: Reverse-complement a DNA strand
goals.why: Strand orientation changes how nucleotide sequences map to biological coordinates.
explain: Complement A↔T and C↔G, preserve N, then reverse the order. Complement-only is not reverse-complement.
Reversing without complementing silently changes the biological sequence interpretation.
The inputs are deliberately synthetic for practice; matching an expected result does not validate a biological interpretation.

worked_example.predict: Why does the result reverse the order as well as the letters?

goals.prediction_answer: The reverse-complement 5′→3′ representation requires both operations.
walkthrough: Complement A↔T and C↔G, preserve N, then reverse the order. Complement-only is not reverse-complement.
Combine a 5-character translation table with slicing [::-1].
Why must strand orientation be recorded alongside a genomic interval?

goals.title: Translate a coding sequence explicitly
goals.why: Coding-frame errors can produce a plausible-looking but incorrect protein.
explain: Biopython Seq.translate() uses a genetic code. State the reading frame and expose incomplete codons rather than silently truncating.
A stop codon and an ambiguous codon are not equivalent: '*' denotes stop; 'X' may represent unknown amino acid.
The inputs are deliberately synthetic for practice; matching an expected result does not validate a biological interpretation.

goals.prediction_answer: MA*; the stop codon is represented by '*'.
